**Test image summary:**
- Stem at a branch junction
- Long, narrow, ELONGATED LINEAR OPEN CANKER running along the stem axis
- Dark brown/reddish-brown center
- White/bleached pale tissue flanking both sides of the lesion
- Otherwise green, healthy-looking stem
- No visible mycelium or spores

**Comparison results:**
| Class | Match |
|---|---|
| Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato | Strong — known for elongated open stem cankers with pale/white margins |
| Gray_Mold | Partial — node lesion (1573933) has similar dark necrosis but Gray Mold typically shows gray fuzzy mycelium |
| Late_Blight | Weak — diffuse dark oily blotches, not this defined open canker |
| Phytophthora_Blight | Weak — dark gray surface discoloration, lacks the white-margin pattern |
| Early_Blight | Weak — circular concentrated canker, not elongated linear |
| Verticillium_Wilt | Weak — internal vascular discoloration, not this surface canker |
| All others | Not matching stem canker pattern |

The elongated, longitudinal open canker with a dark brown center and white/bleached lateral margins is the defining symptom of **Bacterial Canker** (*Clavibacter michiganensis* subsp. *michiganensis*). The open, split-like appearance with pale tissue on the sides running along the stem length is precisely what distinguishes this disease on tomato stems.
